messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: writing '\0' in command.hpp
parts:
Sorry for not code reviewing this more the first time, but
I'm continuing to look at command.hpp and see this:

void write_stan(std::ostream* s, const char prefix = '\0') {
if(!s) return;

*s << prefix << " stan_version_major = " << stan::MAJOR_VERSION << std::endl;
*s << prefix << " stan_version_minor = " << stan::MINOR_VERSION << std::endl;
*s << prefix << " stan_version_patch = " << stan::PATCH_VERSION << std::endl;

}

You really don't want to be writing '\0' out. It's the
plain-old C string terminator character 0.

Following advice from here:

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/14795565/difference-between-null-terminated-char-0-and

I wrote this little C++ program:


#include <iostream>

int main() {
std::cout << '\0' << "abc" << std::endl;
}

which produces this:

~/temp2$ clang++ pound.cpp
~/temp2$ ./a.out | hexdump -C
00000000 00 61 62 63 0a |.abc.|
00000005

You see the '\0' written out as the first hex value 00, then
the "abc" as 61, 62, and 63, then the newline as 0a.

If you just print without piping through hexdump, the '\0' disappears,
but apparently that behavior isn't cross-platform.

But the only time write_stan() gets called in our code base,
it's called with prefix = '#'. So why not default to '#' and
then not include the '#' in the call?

I think it's better to not try to guess at how to make functions
like this flexible before we have a use for that flexibility.

If you want configurable prefixes, use strings and default
to the empty string.

void write_stan(std::ostream* s, const char* prefix = "") {
if (!s) return;
*s << prefix << "stan_version_major = " << stan::MAJOR_VERSION
<< std::endl
<< prefix << "stan_version_minor = " << stan::MINOR_VERSION
<< std::endl
<< prefix << "stan_version_patch = " << stan::PATCH_VERSION
<< std::endl;
}

and then call it with:

write_stan(s, "# ");

You probably don't want to assume an initial space if there's not a prefix.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] writing '\0' in command.hpp
parts:
Make it an issue. This is actually more expansive, as the behavior
here is meant to mirror the behavior in the arg code. I originally
went with a single char to enforce the prefix being a single
character long, and '\0' is the closest thing to an empty char.
I'll change everything to strings and just allow prefixes of any size.
